output.summary: A grapevine native to Asia, the Amur grape withstands severe frost but not drought. Its berries range from very acidic to sweet, and ripe fruit can be eaten raw or made into wine, juice, jellies and jams; the leaves are used in salad.
output.edibilityNote: Ripe grapes are eaten raw; unripe fruit is acidic and bitter. Fruit is made into wine, juice, jellies and jams; leaves are used in salad.
